ImageDescription.value:
Portrait of Guru Gobind Singh blessing the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones) with Amrit.

Original auction source: [1]

Guru Govind Singh sprinkling his followers with amrit, Punjab, circa 1870.

pen and ink, watercolour and gold on paper, black and orange borders, the paper on the backboard of each inscribed with a description of the scene in a 19th Century hand in English, framed 247 x 333 mm.(4)

Footnotes

Inscription on the reverse: The third deals with the first 'Pahal' or sacrament of the Sikhs.

Guru Govind Singh [...] took an iron basin containing sugar and water which he afterwards called 'Amrit' from his wife who happened to be passing and stirring the mixture with a dagger administered it to his followers who at the same time became Govindi Sikhs by taking the oath of the 5 K's, i.e. Kesh, Kara, Kirpan, Kachda and Khanga i.e. always to wear trousers and not a waistcloth; to wear their hair long and do it up in a knot; to always carry a dagger; to wear a bangle of steel, that being the soldier's metal to symbolise bravery, devotion and trustiness; to wear a comb in their hair.
